doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The open early room, benches, deli lunches and Don Costa's lamps
summary: The early Englewood Cliffs studio had no isolation booths or down lights, and Don Costa bought stand lights.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: When you first moved in it was just all open.
Yeah, there were no isolation booths in the beginning, just a space. Then

Yeah, there were benches all along the periphery for them to sit. Often they’d come with deli lunchmeat and spread it all out on the benches and eat and play and make good records. There were no down lights either in the early days, just those up lights.
They weren’t reading music were they?
Yeah, sure they were. Great stuff, of course!
So how long did it take to put in down lights?

Well Don Costa, I remember he did a couple of sessions here, he went out and he bought me stand lights. Don Coast bought me those! (Laughs) They couldn’t see anything cause it was dark! It was a really… Talk about making mistakes (Laughs). Oh boy.
